headline: Highest risk is medium: OpenMetadata can ingest and expose shared metadata while Whisper is local-only, so prompt injection and leakage are limited but not absent via shared workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata can consume APIs, events, webhooks, and MCP tools, so it may ingest content that later reaches Whisper through a shared workflow. Whisper has no tool use or output-parsing defenses documented, but its local CLI-style model limits direct hijack paths. Because the interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced, uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata forwards untrusted metadata or webhook payloads into a prompt or transcript consumed by Whisper, injection becomes plausible.
IF the two agents are bridged by manual copy-paste or a shared message queue, attacker-controlled text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Add a strict allowlist for fields passed from OpenMetadata to Whisper.
Strip instructions and markup from any text before transcription or downstream parsing.
Require human review of any OpenMetadata-generated text before it is reused.
Use separate queues or topics for machine-generated content and user content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every payload crossing the pair.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data, while Whisper only processes audio files and has no network egress or filesystem write. The pair does not show a shared workspace or authenticated cloud path, so leakage is limited to unusual operator wiring rather than default behavior. The main risk is accidental exposure of sensitive metadata in copied transcripts.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata exports sensitive metadata into audio transcripts or text files later fed to Whisper, those contents can be exposed in downstream logs or outputs.
IF an operator manually copies confidential catalog text into Whisper inputs, leakage occurs through the workflow.
mitigations: Keep sensitive catalog exports out of Whisper inputs.
Use redacted samples when testing the pair.
Disable any shared folder or clipboard bridge between the tools.
Review transcripts before storing them alongside governance data.
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive and non-sensitive datasets at the orchestration layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata advertises APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP, but Whisper has no filesystem write, git, shell, or network egress capabilities. There is no overlapping mutable resource or write surface in the profiles, so a direct capability conflict is not plausible from the documented surfaces. Uncertainty is low because Whisper is explicitly constrained.
conditions: IF Whisper is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants it write or git privileges, conflict risk would change.
IF OpenMetadata and Whisper are both given write access to the same mutable store outside these profiles, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep Whisper read-only and offline.
Do not grant shared write access to any workspace.
Run OpenMetadata and Whisper under separate service accounts.
Avoid mounting the same mutable directory into both runtimes.
requires-engineering: add locking if a shared store is introduced later.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can produce governance and lineage outputs that a downstream system may treat as authoritative, while Whisper can turn audio into text without verification. If Whisper consumes OpenMetadata-generated text or if OpenMetadata ingests Whisper transcripts as facts, errors can cascade across work products. The pair lacks a built-in verification step, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are used as authoritative metadata in OpenMetadata, transcription errors can propagate into catalog records.
IF OpenMetadata-generated descriptions are fed into Whisper-based workflows without verification, downstream actions may rely on incorrect facts.
mitigations: Require human verification before publishing any Whisper-derived text in OpenMetadata.
Mark machine-generated fields as untrusted until reviewed.
Compare Whisper output against source audio for critical records.
Limit automatic ingestion to low-risk metadata only.
requires-engineering: add a validation gate between transcription and catalog publication.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance and memory/tribal knowledge, which can include regulated or sensitive data, while Whisper is local-only and handles audio files without network egress. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to operator-managed data handling rather than an inherent pairwise breach. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pair's data flow.
conditions: IF regulated audio or metadata is routed from OpenMetadata into Whisper and then stored without the required retention controls, compliance obligations may be missed.
IF the operator uses the pair on PHI or EU PII without a documented policy, residency and retention review is required.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it through the pair.
Avoid using regulated data in test runs.
Document retention for Whisper outputs and OpenMetadata records.
Restrict access to governance exports.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for residency and retention before ingestion.
